input: How do I create a new Git branch?
expected: Use: git checkout -b <branch>. This creates and switches to the branch based on your current HEAD.

input: How do I open a pull request on GitHub?
expected: Push your feature branch to GitHub, then on the repo page click Compare & pull request → add title/description → Create pull request.

input: How do I delete a local Git branch?
expected: Run: git branch -d <branch> (or -D to force) while checked out on a different branch.

input: How can I rename a Git branch?
expected: Rename the current branch: git branch -m <new-name>. Rename another: git branch -m <old> <new>.

input: How do I set up SSH keys for GitHub?
expected: Generate with ssh-keygen -t ed25519; copy the public key; on GitHub → Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key → paste and save.

input: How do I resolve merge conflicts?
expected: Open conflicted files, keep the desired changes, remove conflict markers, then git add and git commit to complete the merge.

input: How do I fork a repository on GitHub?
expected: Click Fork on the repo page, choose your account/org, then clone your fork locally.

input: Create a new branch in Git
expected: git checkout -b <branch>. Push with git push -u origin <branch> if you want to publish it.

input: How do I clone a repository with HTTPS?
expected: Use git clone https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git. Provide credentials if prompted.

input: How do I change the last commit message?
expected: Run git commit --amend. Edit the message and save; avoid amending commits that are already pushed/shared.

input: How do I enable two-factor authentication (2FA) on GitHub?
expected: GitHub → Settings → Password and authentication → Two-factor authentication → Set up with an authenticator app or SMS and store recovery codes.

input: Create a pull request on GitHub
expected: On the repository page, click Compare & pull request from your branch, review changes, then Create pull request.

input: How do I add a collaborator to my repository?
expected: Repo → Settings → Collaborators and teams → Add people → enter the username and set permissions.

input: How do I make a repository private?
expected: Repo → Settings → General → Danger Zone → Change visibility → Private → confirm.

input: How long do classic personal access tokens last on GitHub?
expected: Personal access tokens created with classic scopes expire after 30 days by default.

input: How do I squash commits before merging?
expected: Use git rebase -i <base> and squash (s) the commits you want; or use the Squash and merge option in the PR UI.

input: Remove a local branch in Git
expected: Switch off the branch, then run git branch -d <branch> (or -D to force).

input: How do I delete a remote branch?
expected: Use git push origin --delete <branch> or the GitHub branches UI → Delete.

input: Turn on 2FA for my GitHub account
expected: Go to Settings → Password and authentication → Two-factor authentication → choose an app or SMS and save recovery codes.

input: Add an SSH key to my GitHub account
expected: Generate or copy your public key, then GitHub → Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key → paste and save.

input: Open a PR from a feature branch
expected: Push your branch and click Compare & pull request → fill details → Create pull request.

input: Change repository visibility to private
expected: Settings → General → Change visibility → Private → acknowledge the warnings to confirm.

input: How do I revert a commit?
expected: Use git revert <sha> to create a new commit that undoes the changes. Push the new commit.

input: How do I ignore files with .gitignore?
expected: Create or edit .gitignore with patterns, then remove already-tracked files using git rm -r --cached <path> if needed.

input: How do I transfer a repository to an organization?
expected: Repo → Settings → General → Transfer ownership → type the repo name and target org; you need permissions in the destination org.
